accepted.s: Remote sensing of the Earth's surface primarily involves obtaining information through:
o: Measurement of underground seismic waves alone
Physical contact with the surface only
Collection of soil samples from selected locations
Reflected or emitted radiation without physical contact
accepted.x: Remote sensing obtains information about the Earth's surface without physical contact by detecting reflected or emitted radiation.
accepted.tq: Use the definition and distinguish remote observation from direct physical measurement.
accepted.sec: Remote sensing in disaster management - can/cannot monitor, satellites, fire hotspots, DMS  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly distinguishes passive remote sensing from active remote sensing?
o: Passive sensors detect naturally available radiation, whereas active sensors transmit their own signal.
Passive sensors operate only at night, whereas active sensors operate only during the day.
Passive sensors emit radar signals, whereas active sensors depend only on sunlight.
Both passive and active sensors depend exclusively on solar radiation.
accepted.x: Passive remote sensing uses naturally available radiation such as solar radiation, while active systems transmit their own signal. Resourcesat and Oceansat illustrate passive applications, whereas RISAT uses radar.
accepted.tq: Discriminate paired concepts by their defining operational difference.
accepted.sec: Remote sensing in disaster management - can/cannot monitor, satellites, fire hotspots, DMS  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Consider the following pairs:
1. Resourcesat — Passive remote sensing
2. Oceansat — Passive remote sensing
3. RISAT — Active radar remote sensing
Which of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
accepted.x: Resourcesat and Oceansat use naturally available radiation in passive remote sensing, while RISAT employs its own radar signal and is an active system.
accepted.tq: Check each technology against the defining feature of passive or active sensing.
accepted.sec: Remote sensing in disaster management - can/cannot monitor, satellites, fire hotspots, DMS  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which satellite-system combination is correctly matched with its disaster-management application?
o: Cartosat — Detection of human disease spread
accepted.x: RISAT/SAR can support flood mapping even through cloud cover. INSAT-3DS is used for cyclone tracking, Oceansat for ocean-state information and Cartosat for damage mapping.
accepted.tq: Start from the sure satellite–application pair and eliminate mismatched uses.
accepted.sec: Remote sensing in disaster management - can/cannot monitor, satellites, fire hotspots, DMS  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Bhuvan combines inputs from RISAT/SAR and INSAT-3DS primarily to provide:
o: Individual medical diagnoses in remote areas
accepted.x: Bhuvan combines RISAT/SAR flood-related imagery and INSAT-3DS cyclone-track information to support flood-inundation mapping and cyclone warnings.
accepted.tq: Link the satellite input to the stated decision-support output.
accepted.sec: Remote sensing in disaster management - can/cannot monitor, satellites, fire hotspots, DMS  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding disaster applications of satellites:
1. Oceansat provides information related to ocean state.
2. Cartosat can be used for damage mapping.
3. INSAT-3DS is used for tracking cyclones.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: Oceansat supports ocean-state observations, Cartosat supports damage mapping, and INSAT-3DS supports cyclone tracking; all three statements are correct.
accepted.tq: Verify each statement against the specific application of the named satellite.
accepted.sec: Remote sensing in disaster management - can/cannot monitor, satellites, fire hotspots, DMS  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Fire hotspots are primarily detected by which of the following sensor and satellite combinations?
o: Thermal-infrared sensors on MODIS and VIIRS satellites
Ultrasonic sensors on Cartosat and Oceansat
Optical sensors on communication satellites only
Seismic sensors on INSAT-3DS and RISAT
accepted.x: Fire hotspots are detected using thermal-infrared sensors, particularly MODIS on NASA's Terra and Aqua satellites and VIIRS on Suomi-NPP.
accepted.tq: Match the environmental phenomenon with the appropriate sensing band and platform.
accepted.sec: Remote sensing in disaster management - can/cannot monitor, satellites, fire hotspots, DMS  [APPSC]

accepted.s: MODIS and VIIRS data used for fire-hotspot monitoring are received in India at the Earth station located at:
accepted.x: Fire-hotspot data from MODIS and VIIRS are received at NRSC's Shadnagar Earth station and passed to the Forest Survey of India alert system.
accepted.tq: Test the precise location associated with a data-reception function.
accepted.sec: Remote sensing in disaster management - can/cannot monitor, satellites, fire hotspots, DMS  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The fire-hotspot data received at Shadnagar are passed to which organisation's alert system?
accepted.x: The data are passed to the Forest Survey of India alert system for forest-fire monitoring.
accepted.tq: Use the institutional-role trap by distinguishing data reception from alert generation.
accepted.sec: Remote sensing in disaster management - can/cannot monitor, satellites, fire hotspots, DMS  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
With reference to the Disaster Management Support Programme of ISRO, consider the following statements:
1. It uses INSAT and IRS systems for warning and damage assessment.
2. It is listed among the applications of INSAT.
3. It supplies satellite imaging and communication support for several disasters.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: The DMS Programme uses INSAT and IRS, is recognised as an INSAT application, and provides satellite imaging and communication support for floods, cyclones, droughts, fires, landslides and earthquakes.
accepted.tq: Test multiple institutional functions through a coded statement combination.
accepted.sec: Remote sensing in disaster management - can/cannot monitor, satellites, fire hotspots, DMS  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which of the following is NOT an identified research and development area under ISRO's Disaster Management Support Programme?
accepted.x: Cyclone prediction, coastal vulnerability and landslide early warning are identified DMS research areas. Manufacture of commercial passenger aircraft is not a DMS research area.
accepted.tq: Find the one option outside the stated disaster-management domain.
accepted.sec: Remote sensing in disaster management - can/cannot monitor, satellites, fire hotspots, DMS  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The Decision Support Centre and the National Database for Emergency Management are located at:
accepted.x: The Decision Support Centre and NDEM are housed at NRSC, Hyderabad. The centre acts as a single window for satellite inputs during disasters.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the location of the coordinating centre from other major space institutions.
accepted.sec: Remote sensing in disaster management - can/cannot monitor, satellites, fire hotspots, DMS  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The National Database for Emergency Management (NDEM) is best described as:
o: A GIS repository covering the full disaster-management cycle
A database exclusively for census enumeration
A communication network used only for television broadcasting
A satellite launch vehicle tracking system
accepted.x: NDEM is a GIS repository designed to support the full disaster-management cycle.
accepted.tq: Expand the official acronym by identifying its functional description.
accepted.sec: Remote sensing in disaster management - can/cannot monitor, satellites, fire hotspots, DMS  [APPSC]

accepted.s: During a disaster, the Decision Support Centre of NRSC functions primarily as:
o: A single window for satellite inputs
A laboratory for manufacturing radar chips
A launch site for polar satellites
A centre for issuing driving licences
accepted.x: The Decision Support Centre acts as a single window for satellite inputs required during disasters.
accepted.tq: Identify the operational role of the institution rather than its name alone.
accepted.sec: Remote sensing in disaster management - can/cannot monitor, satellites, fire hotspots, DMS  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following statements regarding access to satellite data for disaster management is correct?
o: Satellite data are released only after the disaster-management cycle ends.
States are prohibited from using satellite data during disasters.
States must request the relevant satellite data from NRSC.
Only foreign agencies can request Indian satellite data.
accepted.x: States must request satellite data from NRSC for disaster-management purposes.
accepted.tq: Apply the institutional-authority test: identify who supplies the requested data.
accepted.sec: Remote sensing in disaster management - can/cannot monitor, satellites, fire hotspots, DMS  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Microwave or Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) remote sensing is especially useful during floods because it can:
o: Operate through cloud cover and in darkness
Replace all ground surveys under every condition
Predict the exact time of an earthquake
accepted.x: Microwave/SAR systems can observe through cloud cover and in darkness, making them useful for flood mapping during cloudy conditions.
accepted.tq: Use the practical advantage of the technology to solve the stated disaster scenario.
accepted.sec: Remote sensing in disaster management - can/cannot monitor, satellites, fire hotspots, DMS  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Assam's proposal to use SAR satellites for flood-related observation is particularly relevant because the State is cloudy for approximately:
accepted.x: Assam is reported to be cloudy for about half the year; SAR is useful because it can observe through cloud cover.
accepted.tq: Test the approximate quantitative figure and connect it with the technology's advantage.
accepted.sec: Remote sensing in disaster management - can/cannot monitor, satellites, fire hotspots, DMS  [APPSC]

accepted.s: InSAR is used in remote sensing primarily to:
o: Map ground deformation by comparing radar images
Transmit cyclone warnings through television towers
Measure only ocean salinity from optical images
Identify crop diseases through manual inspection
accepted.x: InSAR, or Interferometric SAR, maps ground deformation by comparing radar images of the Earth's surface.
accepted.tq: Break the technical term into its component parts and identify its use.
accepted.sec: Remote sensing in disaster management - can/cannot monitor, satellites, fire hotspots, DMS  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements about NISAR:
1. It can detect ground movement to the centimetre scale.
2. It has applications in studying land subsidence, earthquakes and glaciers.
3. It depends exclusively on visible-light images and cannot use radar observations.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: NISAR can detect centimetre-scale ground movement and is useful for land subsidence, earthquakes and glaciers. Statement 3 is false because NISAR uses radar observations.
accepted.tq: Reject the extreme and technically reversed statement while retaining the supported applications.
accepted.sec: Remote sensing in disaster management - can/cannot monitor, satellites, fire hotspots, DMS  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the role of the International Charter Space and Major Disasters?
o: It coordinates space-based support during major disasters.
It prepares India's annual Union Budget.
It certifies all weather instruments sold in India.
It regulates commercial airline ticket prices.
accepted.x: The International Charter Space and Major Disasters provides space-based support for major disasters. ISRO took the lead role for six months from April 2025.
accepted.tq: Identify the function of an international mechanism from its institutional title.
accepted.sec: Remote sensing in disaster management - can/cannot monitor, satellites, fire hotspots, DMS  [APPSC]

accepted.s: ISRO took the lead role in the International Charter Space and Major Disasters for six months beginning in:
accepted.x: ISRO assumed the lead role in the International Charter Space and Major Disasters for six months from April 2025.
accepted.tq: Test the precise commencement date using closely spaced year options.
accepted.sec: Remote sensing in disaster management - can/cannot monitor, satellites, fire hotspots, DMS  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which sequence correctly represents the communication chain in the INSAT Disaster Warning System?
o: Coastal receiver → C-band uplink → Cyclone Warning Centre, Chennai → S-band downlink
Cyclone Warning Centre, Chennai → C-band uplink → S-band downlink → coastal receivers
S-band uplink → NRSC, Hyderabad → C-band downlink → inland receivers
Forest Survey of India → optical uplink → INSAT-3DS → ocean receivers
accepted.x: The system follows the chain: Cyclone Warning Centre at Chennai, C-band uplink, S-band downlink and reception by coastal disaster-warning receivers.
accepted.tq: Follow the first-to-last communication sequence and eliminate reversed links.
accepted.sec: Remote sensing in disaster management - can/cannot monitor, satellites, fire hotspots, DMS  [APPSC]

o: Bhoonidhi — Archive and hub for Indian and foreign Earth-observation data since 1988
MOSDAC — Property cards for rural households

accepted.s:
Match List-I with List-II:
List-I (Portal or service)
a. Bhuvan Panchayat
b. Yuktdhara
c. SVAMITVA
 d. PM Gati Shakti
List-II (Primary use)
i. National Master Plan GIS platform

Detection of forest fires through MODIS
accepted.x: SVAMITVA involves drone mapping of rural inhabited properties in association with the Survey of India and supports the issue of property cards.

o: It plans and monitors MGNREGA assets for Gram Panchayats.
It functions as a coastal cyclone-warning receiver.
It prepares property cards through urban cadastral surveys alone.
It provides only foreign Earth-observation data acquired before 1988.
